facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 12 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 26 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 10 March 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 29 December 2013.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
Each applicant attended one of the demonstrations as specified in the Appendix.
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
All the applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
All the applicants were taken to various police stations following their arrest.
On the day of each applicant's arrest, administrative offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued.
The administrative offence reports stated that the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The first-instance courts found that the applicants had participated in unauthorised demonstrations.
The applicants were convicted under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicants were sentenced to a period of administrative detention varying from thirteen to seventeen days, or to a fine of 400 or 500 Azerbaijani manats (AZN), as specified in the Appendix.
It appears that the organisers of the demonstrations gave no proper prior notice to the relevant authority, the Baku City Executive Authority.

At the time of the applicants' arrest, Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences on breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, punishments in the form of administrative detention of up to 15 days were introduced for the first time under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Following the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was increased to between AZN 300 and AZN 600 for participants of an assembly.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', noted that there is no political dialogue with the opposition parties outside parliament in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive climate for the activities of the extra-parliamentary opposition in Azerbaijan, which complains about limitations imposed on freedom of expression and freedom of assembly and the lack of access to the public media.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the establishment of an inclusive political system and a truly competitive and unrestrictive political environment requires full implementation of basic freedoms, including freedom of expression, freedom of assembly and freedom of association.
Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed deep concern about the situation regarding basic freedoms in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe noted that recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, 'unauthorised' gatherings.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe noted that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in 'unauthorised' gatherings are likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about the restrictive use of certain articles of the Criminal Code, in particular Articles 221 and 233, against participants in peaceful, albeit unauthorised, demonstrations.

In Report (CommDH(2013)14), the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe expressed deep concern about recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly in Azerbaijan.

In Report (CommDH(2013)14), the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations.

In Report (CommDH(2013)14), the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe expressed the view that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

In Report (CommDH(2013)14), the Commissioner for Human Rights of the Council of Europe urged the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
